alignments.note: Hortatory subjunctive with its auxiliary Let and subject us, discontinuous under rule 15; head on the lexical verb.
μηκέτι rendered by the discontinuous not … any more; head on the temporal element rather than the negative prefix (rules 15, 17, 66). A head on not remains defensible.
Reciprocal ἀλλήλους → one another, headed on the ἄλλος-word (rule 83).
Imperative with its supplied subject pronoun (rules 7, 9).
Nominalizing article of the articular infinitive; English writes no word for it (rule 61).
μή carries the clause's negation as no; the following man is supplied and is no negative indefinite, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question.

Infinitive expanded into a finite clause: the complementizer that belongs to the expanded complement (rule 85) and the supplied subject man is a rule 74 helper on the infinitive. Keeping no man whole on μή remains defensible.
Anarthrous noun with its supplied indefinite determiner (rule 51).

No possessor stands in the Greek, so the supplied his is the article's (rule 20); the complex frame in … way rides with the determiner-bearing article and heads on its own determiner (rule 67). Putting in … way on the noun remains defensible.
σκάνδαλον → an occasion of falling; occasion is the generic frame noun and falling carries the lexeme's sense (rules 17, 66). A head on occasion remains defensible.

review_notes: The negation no is split from the supplied subject man, the latter being the infinitive's argument under rule 74; the competing reading keeps no man whole on μή.
The head of σκάνδαλον's phrase is contested and is recorded in the unit's note.
